title: Not one tear, not one kindness, falls off His count
subtitle: Al-Muhsi: the One who counts and keeps every single thing, so nothing you do is ever lost
intro: Al-Muhsi (الْمُحْصِي) means the All-Counting, the Enumerator: the One who has counted every created thing, every breath, raindrop and deed, precisely and without error or forgetting. It means no good you do is ever too small to be kept, and no wrong done to you slips off the record.

root.sense: Hasa means pebbles. The Arabs once counted with small stones, laying one down for each item, so ihsa' came to mean counting something completely, one by one, until nothing is left out. Al-Muhsi counts every single thing in creation, individually, with nothing missed.

knowing: Al-Muhsi has counted all things in number (72:28). Not roughly, not by category, but one by one: every grain of sand, every drop of rain, every heartbeat of every creature that ever lived. {idea}He does not estimate. He knows the exact count of everything.{/idea} He has enumerated them and counted them a full counting (19:94).

This name sits inside Al-Alim, His all-embracing knowledge, but it adds precision. Al-Alim knows everything; Al-Muhsi knows the exact number and detail of every individual thing. It also stands beside Al-Hasib, the Reckoner: Al-Muhsi keeps the full record, and Al-Hasib brings it to account and is enough for His servants.

There is a striking contrast in the Quran. If you tried to count the blessings of Allah, you could never enumerate them (14:34, 16:18). The same verb is used. {idea}We cannot count His gifts to us, yet He counts every deed of ours.{/idea} Our counting fails at the first step; His never fails at all.
seeing: Everything is recorded: all things We have enumerated in writing (78:29), in a clear register (36:12). On the Day of Judgement people will open their book and say: what kind of book is this that leaves out nothing small or great, but has counted it (18:49)? They will find everything they did present before them.
Allah will raise them all and tell them what they did. He counted it, while they forgot it (58:6). We forget what we said last week. He has kept every word of every year.

The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah has ninety-nine names, and whoever ahsaha them will enter Paradise (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). The verb is from this same root. Scholars explain it as learning them, understanding them and living by them. The One who counts everything invites us to count, and treasure, His names.
trusting: Much of our discouragement is the feeling that our effort disappears. You were patient with a difficult parent, you swallowed an insult, you gave quietly, and nothing seemed to come of it. {reward}Al-Muhsi counted every one.{/reward} Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (99:7). Nothing you do for Him is ever too small to be kept.

It also lifts the burden of keeping score with people. You do not need to remember every slight or keep a tally of who owes you. Al-Muhsi keeps the record perfectly. You can forgive, move on and let Him hold the account.

And it keeps you honest about the small wrongs. {trap}Thinking a glance, a white lie or a careless word does not count{/trap} is how the record fills up unnoticed. An atom's weight of harm will also be seen (99:8). Counting your own deeds now, gently and honestly, is better than being surprised by them later.
loving: There is tenderness in being counted. A mother knows how many children she has and notices if one is missing. Al-Muhsi knows each one of His servants by name and number. {idea}You are not a statistic to Him; you are counted individually.{/idea}
And when you realise you cannot even count His blessings, while He carefully counts every small good you do, gratitude turns into love.
now: It is payday, and after rent and bills there is almost nothing left. You still put a few coins in the charity box on your way home, embarrassed at how little it is. {reward}Al-Muhsi counted it exactly, and the sincerity behind it too.{/reward} Walk home lighter; nothing given for Him is too small to be kept.
old: My small efforts are so tiny they do not really make a difference.
new: Al-Muhsi counts every single deed, so even an atom of good I do is kept.
try: Tonight, before you sleep, count three blessings from today and one small good you did, and thank Al-Muhsi for both.

dua.text: Ya Muhsi, You have counted my every deed while I forgot them. Count my small good with mercy, erase my wrongs, and let me never belittle a kindness.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when your efforts feel worthless or when you review your day, remembering that He has counted all things in number (72:28).

pairs.why: Al-Muhsi keeps the complete record; Al-Hasib brings it to account and is sufficient for His servants.
Al-Alim knows everything; Al-Muhsi knows it in exact number and detail, one by one.
Al-Muhsi counts even the smallest deed; Ash-Shakur appreciates it and rewards it many times over.

faq.a: Al-Muhsi means the All-Counting, the Enumerator. Allah has counted every created thing and every deed individually and exactly, with nothing missed or forgotten. The Quran describes Him with this verb in verses like 72:28, 19:94 and 58:6.

faq.q: Is Al-Muhsi mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: The exact form Al-Muhsi is not used as a name in the Quran, but the Quran describes Allah with its verb several times, saying He has counted all things in number. The name appears in the well-known list of ninety-nine names narrated by at-Tirmidhi.

faq.q: What does it mean to ahsa the 99 names?
faq.a: In the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, whoever ahsaha the ninety-nine names enters Paradise. The word comes from the same root as Al-Muhsi. Scholars explain it as learning the names, understanding their meanings, calling on Allah by them and living by what they teach.
